title: QBR health signal exploration & scoring lab
content:
Purpose / context:
This is a working lab document—notes from QBR signal brainstorming session (11/04/2025) plus a first-pass scoring worksheet and operational playbook mappings. Goal: propose a compact, explainable health score used inside QBRs and renewal prep that highlights top risk drivers (not just a single opaque number). Keep it human-readable for CSMs and compatible with downstream analytics (SQL, dbt).

High-level requirements (what we need from the model):
- Interpretable: each score component maps to a tangible signal and recommended action.
- Lightweight: can be computed from event stream + billing + support tables daily.
- Tunable: weights easy to change per customer segment (SMB / Mid / Enterprise).
- Actionable thresholds: red/yellow/green with recommended playbook steps.
- Handles missing data: fallbacks and imputation notes.

Primary signal groups (candidate list & quick defs):
1) Usage and adoption (45% baseline weight)
   - active-users-weekly: unique users with any API call in last 7 days
   - routes-used: number of distinct Redwood endpoints the customer calls (chat/generate/embeddings)
   - peak-concurrency: 95th pct usage per minute — proxy for scaling needs
   - embed-rate: embeddings calls per seat-week (adoption of semantic features)

2) Quality & outcome signals (20%)
   - eval-regressions: count of failing evals (defined prompt sets) over last 30 days
   - customer-escalations: severity >= P2 incidents opened this quarter
   - manual-review-rate: fraction of outputs flagged for review/rollback

3) Support & satisfaction (15%)
   - ticket-volume-normalized: tickets per active-user-week
   - sla-breaches: incidents that missed target response/resolve times
   - recent-nps: latest NPS numeric if available (fall back to CSAT snippets)

4) Commercial signals (10%)
   - invoice-past-due: boolean + days-past due bucketed
   - usage-trend-vs-commit: percent difference vs committed baseline

5) Product health / config (10%)
   - stale-model-pin: customer pinned to model older than 6 months (risk for regressions)
   - caching-enabled: boolean (true is positive)
   - telemetry-integrations: presence of observability/tracing (good)

Scoring approach (simple, transparent):
- Each signal normalized to 0..100 where higher = healthier (we invert risk signals).
- Weighted sum: Health = sum(weight_i * normalized_signal_i) / sum(weights) -> 0..100
- Buckets: 0-49 RED, 50-74 YELLOW, 75-100 GREEN

Normalization notes / example transforms:
- active-users-weekly: norm = min(100, log(1 + value) / log(1 + target) * 100) where target = segment median active users
- ticket-volume-normalized: norm = 100 - min(100, tickets_per_user_week * 200) (tickets are negative)
- invoice-past-due: 0 if overdue > 0 else 100
- recent-nps: scaled from -100..100 to 0..100 via (nps + 100)/2

Missing data handling:
- If eval-regressions missing -> assume 100 (optimistic) but set a confidence flag.
- If NPS missing and ticket tone negative (text heuristics) -> map tone to NPS proxy.
- Keep a confidence score per customer as fraction of signals present; expose to CSMs as transparency metric.

Quick scoring worksheet (toy customer: Acme Widget Co):
- active-users-weekly = 12; target for mid-market = 20 -> normalized 60
- routes-used = 1 (only chat) -> normalized 40 (low diversification)
- peak-concurrency = 120 rps (target 200) -> normalized 60
- combined usage (weighted subset) -> usage_subscore = 0.45*(60+40+60)/3 = 27
- eval-regressions = 3 failing evals/30 days -> normalized 20 -> quality_subscore = 0.20*20 = 4
- ticket-volume-normalized = 0.08 tickets/user/week -> normalized 92 -> support_subscore = 0.15*92 = 13.8
- invoice-past-due = 0 days -> 100 -> commercial_subscore = 0.10*100 = 10
- caching-enabled = false -> product_subscore = 0.10*30 = 3 (penalty for no cache)
- Raw health = 27 + 4 + 13.8 + 10 + 3 = 57.8 -> normalized to 58 -> YELLOW
- Confidence = 8/10 signals present -> display as "58 (conf 80%)"

Playbook mappings (by bucket) — concise steps for CSMs during QBR prep:
- RED (0-49): immediate renewal at-risk playbook
  - 1: Schedule technical deep-dive within 72 hrs with solutions eng. Attach JIRA CS-412
  - 2: Offer short-term burst credit or dedicated tuning session (commercial runway)
  - 3: Mandatory exec touchpoint + updated mitigation timeline in next 7 days
  - 4: Prepare RACI for remediation; escalate to support SRE on call

- YELLOW (50-74): proactive retention playbook
  - 1: Prepare targeted QBR agenda focused on top 3 risk signals
  - 2: Propose adoption nudges: enable caching, route diversification plan, sample prompts
  - 3: Launch a 14-day "eval guardrail" with dataset-based monitoring and weekly check-ins
  - 4: Track conversion of proposed actions -> move to green within 30 days

- GREEN (75-100): expansion + advocacy playbook
  - 1: Identify expansion routes (embeddings, reranking) and send a small pilot proposal
  - 2: Ask for reference / case study if usage exceeds X for 60 days
  - 3: Highlight efficiency wins in QBR (cost/token improvements)

Operational decisions / edge cases:
- Segment-specific weights: enterprise customers get more weight on commercial signals (20% instead of 10%) and lower on active-users (30% instead of 45%).
- Seasonality: normalize active-users to trailing-90-day seasonal baseline to avoid false negatives during planned low-usage periods.
- One-off anomalies: allow manual "score freeze" by CSM when legitimate business change is documented (MOU, pilot cadence change).

Open experiments / TODOs (fast tasks):
- [ ] A/B test weight set A vs B across 200 renewal cases (owner: Rina, JIRA: CS-501)
- [ ] Build SQL materialized view for normalized signals (owner: Liam, GitHub: health-scores/pull/56)
- [ ] Instrument ticket text heuristics (simple sentiment -> NPS proxy) (owner: Ethan)
- [ ] Add confidence column to export used by QBR template (owner: Maya)

Questions we raised in the session:
- Is a single health score helpful or will CSMs prefer a signal vector? (CSM feedback: both — number for sorting, vector for narrative)
- How do we handle customers with intentionally low API usage but high revenue (one-off batch users)? Proposed: revenue-weighted override that flags them for account review rather than auto-red.
- Do we expose the formula to customers? Probably not; give a narrative and top 3 drivers instead.

Appendix: short checklist for QBR prep using the score:
- Pull latest health score + confidence (SQL snapshot)
- Validate any red flags with product/support owners
- Prepare 3 data-backed bullets for QBR (usage trend, top regression, suggested next step)
- Attach action item column with owner and due date in QBR notes

Meeting notes (11/04/2025):
- consensus: keep model simple for launch, then iterate with A/B experiments
- immediate ask: analytics team to provide weekly materialized table by 11/18/2025
- next sync: internal review w/ solutions eng on 11/20/2025 (owner: Maya)

Endnotes / references:
- See Confluence: CONFLUENCE-HealthModel-2847 for full signal dictionary (work in progress)
- Related PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/health-scores/pull/56 (normalization helpers)

Notes to self:
- When presenting to GTM, show 3 anonymized customer examples (green/yellow/red) and the resulting QBR playbooks.
